headline: The investor Chamath Palihapitiya warned that the rush to fund AI infrastructure with private loans could be building a credit bubble.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; it is an investor's opinion in a social media post.
importance_line: Lenders, pension funds and other investors in private credit are most exposed, then AI infrastructure firms that rely on this debt; the doubt is that these are one investor's figures and views.
summary: Open Magazine reports that Chamath Palihapitiya, chief executive of the firms 8090 and Social Capital, wrote on X that the AI build-out is increasingly funded by debt and that private credit, loans made outside the public bond markets, now plays a much larger role. He cited a $35 billion financing led by Apollo and Blackstone to buy chips and lease them to Anthropic, which UBS called the largest private credit deal on record, and said lenders may be underestimating AI risks, equity investors may be overestimating future profits, or both.
notes: The listed India's News.Net page (an ANI relay) was blocked by Cloudflare; the same story was read at Open Magazine. All figures are Palihapitiya's, as cited by Open Magazine; not checked against UBS, S&P Global or the Bank for International Settlements.
